## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-anonymized. The archived guidelines (2025-07-16) say editors first read each manuscript to decide whether it merits being sent to a panel of anonymized reviewers; submissions must conceal identity, affiliations and funding sources, and the title page is a separate upload. Fitness is judged on scope and relevance to education, conceptual framework, methods (fit, description, rigor), whether findings follow from the literature or data, overall contribution, and writing (same page) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. Not stated in the archived guidelines |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. Not stated in the archived guidelines |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Blank. No source found. SciRev has no reviews (https://scirev.org/journal/american-educational-research-journal/) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. The archived guidelines refer reviewers to separate Reviewer Guidelines, which were not read |
| **Grievances** | Authors who believe their manuscript was not reviewed carefully or in a timely way are told to raise it with the association's executive officer or president (archived guidelines, 2025-07-16) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | None found. The archived author guidelines (2025-07-16) contain no AI section (the page text was searched for "artificial", "generative" and "AI"). The publisher-wide Sage policy applies: https://www.sagepub.com/journals/publication-ethics-policies/artificial-intelligence-policy (read through an archived copy dated 2026-11-15) |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate found. Disclosure is required for generative uses |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with disclosure of generative use; same rubric as the Mind entry) |
| **Summary** | Sage policy, paraphrased: assistive tools for language, grammar or structure need no disclosure; generative use that produces text, references, images or other content bearing on methods, analysis, results or conclusions must be disclosed on submission, within the methods or acknowledgements; GenAI should not be cited as a primary source; listed inappropriate uses include fabricated references, interviewing GenAI tools in place of participants, and presenting generated images as research images; a submission is not rejected for disclosed use but may be rejected if undisclosed misuse emerges; reviewers and editors may not paste manuscripts into GenAI tools. Archived copy of 2026-11-15; retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Source URL** | https://www.sagepub.com/journals/publication-ethics-policies/artificial-intelligence-policy |

### Preprint Policy

> Journal guidelines (archived 2025-07-16) plus the Sage prior-publication page (archived copy 2026-11-15, https://www.sagepub.com/journals/publication-ethics-policies/prior-publication) and the Sage archiving page (https://www.sagepub.com/journals/permissions/sages-author-archiving-and-re-use-guidelines, retrieved 2026-11-23). AERJ's copyright is assigned to the association, so whether the Sage-wide archiving page governs this journal is not confirmed.

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| Pre-submission | Conditional | AERJ's guidelines do not accept manuscripts previously published, in press or under consideration elsewhere and point to Sage's prior-publication page. That page lists preprint-server versions as a kind of prior distribution that may be acceptable, asks authors to check each journal's guidelines, says some journals will not consider preprinted work, and warns that for double-anonymized journals a posted preprint may let reviewers discover the author's identity. The AERJ guidelines do not address preprints by name |
| Under review | Blank | The Sage prior-publication page asks authors not to post updated versions until a decision is made |
| Post-acceptance (AAM) | Yes per Sage-wide page | The Sage archiving page says the original submission or accepted manuscript may be shared at any time after acceptance on any website or repository; it states no embargo. Embargo: none stated on that page (not confirmed for this society-owned journal) |
| Version of Record | Restricted | The Sage archiving page says the final published PDF may not be posted on unrestricted sites without permission, and that open-access licences change this |

## Format

> Source: archived copy (2025-07-16) of the Sage author-instructions page for the journal, http://web.archive.org/web/20250716143943/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/AER. The live page returned 403 to curl; a real-browser read on 2026-11-24 confirmed length, abstract and the absence of AI wording only.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Original peer-reviewed analyses across education research, with empirical, theoretical and methodological contributions, all levels of education and forms of learning (aims, https://www.aera.net/Publications/Journals/American-Educational-Research-Journal, retrieved 2026-11-23). The archived guidelines also describe comments on published articles and replies (right of reply). No separate review or short-report type is listed; the association's Review of Educational Research is a separate journal |
| **Word limit** | Counted in pages, not words: the main document may not exceed 50 double-spaced pages including all tables, figures, notes and references, on 8.5 by 11 inch paper with 1-inch margins and 12-point type (Times New Roman preferred) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The guidelines say manuscripts not conforming may be returned; no exceptions are stated. Appendices count toward the 50 pages unless uploaded as online supplementary material |
| **Abstract limit** | 100-120 words; keywords: "a few", with 3 to 5 typical for the association's journals |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap; references count inside the 50 pages. APA 7th edition for style and references; DOIs where available |
| **Supplementary material** | Allowed as separate online files marked "ONLINE SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIALS" at the top and "online" in the file name; not included in print |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Tables go at the end after the references and should be editable Word or Excel; one high-quality file per figure; figures print in grayscale and appear in colour online |
| **Style / submission format** | Submission through Sage's ScholarOne site (https://mc.manuscriptcentral.com/aerj, as stated on the archived page); Word, or LaTeX with the PDF; separate title page with all authors' contact details; notes avoided where possible and placed at the end as plain text; own work cited as "Author, year" and listed first in the reference list; an anonymized response letter on revision |

## Soft Metadata

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

> Evidence layers: OpenAlex keyword counts over 219 abstract-bearing articles (2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23); OpenAlex author-country data for 225 articles; the association's aims and editors pages (retrieved 2026-11-23). Thresholds are this pass's own convention, not an external standard.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Author countries on the 225 articles (OpenAlex; articles with at least one author in the country; 217 carry any country): US 201, CA 6, GB 5, DE 4, CN 3, HK 3, KR 2, CL 2, IL 2, and one each in several others (retrieved 2026-11-23). The association page records a 2015 webinar introducing a "new focus" on research on globally pressing educational issues and inviting international scholars (https://www.aera.net/Publications/Journals/American-Educational-Research-Journal; page text dated March 10, 2015) |
| **Editorial-board geography** | Current 2025-2027 editor team on the association page (https://www.aera.net/Publications/Journals/American-Educational-Research-Journal/AERJ-Editors, retrieved 2026-11-23): 29 entries (1 editor-in-chief, 7 coeditors, 21 associate editors). The page prints a country for 2 entries only, Colombia 1 and Germany 1; the other 27 name US institutions without printing the country (27+1+1 = 29; the US attribution is read from the institution names, not from a printed country). One coeditor is marked on leave. The page lists no separate editorial board. An older Sage board page, archived 2022-12-03 (http://web.archive.org/web/20221203035348/https://journals.sagepub.com/editorial-board/AER), listed 87 entries (1 editor-in-chief, 5 coeditors, 20 associate editors, 1 managing editor, 60 board members) with printed countries USA 84, Canada 2 and one entry with no affiliation (84+2+1 = 87); it predates the current editor team |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | `decoloni\w*` or `indigenous` appear in 6 of 219 abstracts (2.74%); `critical race`, `intersectionalit\w*` or `settler colonial\w*` in 6 (2.74%). No editorial statement on non-Western epistemologies was found on the pages read |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | Counts in 219 abstracts: `racism\|racist\|racial\w*\|whiteness` 56 (25.57%); capitalised Black, Latinx, Latino, Latina or Hispanic 46 (21.00%); `equit(y\|able)` 31 (14.16%); `gender(ed)?` 7 (3.20%); LGBT, queer, transgender or sexual orientation 3 (1.37%). ### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Partly stated. The archived guidelines list the criteria by which fitness is judged: scope and relevance to the field of education, conceptual framework connected to relevant constructs in the literature, methods (appropriateness, description of data collection, samples and analysis, rigor), findings drawn from the literature or data, overall contribution, and writing (http://web.archive.org/web/20250716143943/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/AER, archived 2025-07-16).
- **What kind of engagement?** Empirical, theoretical or methodological advance on education and learning, any level, any subfield or discipline (aims, https://www.aera.net/Publications/Journals/American-Educational-Research-Journal, retrieved 2026-11-23). The association page also records the 2015 invitation to international scholars on globally pressing issues.
- **Article type and length**: up to 50 double-spaced pages including references; abstract 100-120 words; APA 7th edition (archived guidelines).
- **Scope signals in the data**: OpenAlex topic-assignment counts are led by school choice and performance (579), teacher education and leadership (292), achievement (292) and critical race theory in education (250) (Subject Density); `school` appears in 132 of 219 abstracts (60.27%) and `polic(y|ies)` in 64 (29.22%).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: the archived guidelines say submissions not conforming to the guidelines may be returned. No first-hand rejection report was found (SciRev: no reviews, https://scirev.org/journal/american-educational-research-journal/).

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored; no first-person rule found in the archived guidelines. Sample: 119 of 219 abstract-bearing articles (54.3%) contain I, my, we or our in the abstract (regex `\b(I|my|we|our)\b`, case-sensitive; plural "we" may be generic). Of the 10 most recently dated abstract-bearing articles (2026-10-20 to 2026-11-17), 6 contain it: https://doi.org/10.3102/00028312261503324, https://doi.org/10.3102/00028312261501090, https://doi.org/10.3102/00028312261492656, https://doi.org/10.3102/00028312261493445, https://doi.org/10.3102/00028312261489233, https://doi.org/10.3102/00028312261491336; the other 4 do not (for example https://doi.org/10.3102/00028312261502381). OpenAlex works API, retrieved 2026-11-23. The guidelines' own anonymization examples forbid first-person self-reference that reveals the author ("the term I refer as ...") |
| **Expected density** | Up to 50 double-spaced pages including references, tables, figures and notes; abstract 100-120 words (archived guidelines, 2025-07-16) |
| **Writing style notes** | APA 7th edition; subheads at reasonable intervals; abbreviations spelled out at first mention; notes avoided; guidelines ask for good English and point to Sage's language-editing referral page (archived guidelines) |
| **Authorship pattern** | Crossref author lists for 226 of the 235 journal-article records of 2021-01 to 2026-11-23 (https://api.crossref.org/works?filter=issn:0002-8312,from-pub-date:2021-01-01,until-pub-date:2026-11-23): 1 author 43 (19.0%), 2 authors 55, 3 authors 42, 4 or more 86 |

Reviewer behaviour itself is not observable from public pages; what follows is what public pages do show.

No reviewer list or board page current to 2026 could be read; the older Sage board copy listed 87 entries, of which 60 were "Editorial Board" members, mostly at US institutions (USA 84, Canada 2) | https://www.aera.net/Publications/Journals/American-Educational-Research-Journal/AERJ-Editors (retrieved 2026-11-23); older: http://web.archive.org/web/20221203035348/https://journals.sagepub.com/editorial-board/AER |
| **Review model** | Double-anonymized; editors screen, then a panel of anonymized reviewers (number not stated) | http://web.archive.org/web/20250716143943/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/AER (archived 2025-07-16) |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Blank. No first-hand report: SciRev lists no reviews | https://scirev.org/journal/american-educational-research-journal/ |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Blank. No reviewer-level source. Public counts show experimental or randomized terms in 8.68% and interview terms in 11.87% of abstract-bearing articles (regexes in Methodological Preferences), which says nothing about how reviewers treat either | OpenAlex counts, see Methodological Preferences |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | The archived guidelines send authors to the association's Standards for Research Conduct and Code of Ethics (archived 2025-07-16); those documents were not read. Sage's publisher-level policy for humanities and social sciences, which covers education, asks for an "Ethical Considerations" statement on the title page, explains how consent and risk were handled, and treats ethics-committee approval as one possible part of it (https://www.sagepub.com/journals/publication-ethics-policies/research-ethics-policy--humanities-and-social-sciences, retrieved 2026-11-23). Whether AERJ enforces it beyond the guidelines read is not stated |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers are a minority but common: 43 of 226 Crossref records with author lists (19.0%) in 2021-01 to 2026-11-23 |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Sage's policy says it welcomes submissions from independent researchers and may ask for extra information such as underlying data, funding documents, ethics approvals or consent procedures, before or after publication (https://www.sagepub.com/journals/publication-ethics-policies/policy-on-submissions-from-independent-researchers, retrieved 2026-11-23). The association's journal page also reports a 2024 AERJ article by an independent scholar receiving an award (https://www.aera.net/Publications/Journals/American-Educational-Research-Journal, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Data transparency requirement** | No data-sharing requirement found in the archived guidelines. Sage's research-data policy says some journals require data to be shared and points to each journal's guidelines; it encourages data availability statements regardless (https://www.sagepub.com/journals/publication-ethics-policies/research-data-sharing-policies, archived copy 2026-11-15) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-anonymized with a separate title page; manuscripts must hide identity, affiliations and funding; own work is cited as "Author, year"; a response letter must also be anonymized (archived guidelines, 2025-07-16). Sage warns that a posted preprint may reveal the author to reviewers (https://www.sagepub.com/journals/publication-ethics-policies/prior-publication, archived copy 2026-11-15) |
| **AI use** | Publisher-wide Sage policy: disclosure of generative use on submission; assistive language tools exempt (https://www.sagepub.com/journals/publication-ethics-policies/artificial-intelligence-policy, archived copy 2026-11-15) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; the guidelines mention only the Sage Choice route; USD 3,640 for 2026 per Sage's price list (Open Access section); 56 of 225 recent articles are hybrid open access in OpenAlex |

### AI-Research Notes (sources, blanks, and cross-language checks)

**signal_quality (0-5)**: overall 3. Per layer: OpenAlex counts (methods, topics, countries, types) 4 (97.3% abstract coverage over 225 articles; a small journal, so single-digit counts are noisy); Crossref (year counts, author lists) 3; association pages (aims, editors, acceptance reports) 4; author guidelines 3 (archived copy of 2025-07-16, live page unread); publisher-wide policies (AI, preprint, ethics, independent researchers, data, APC list) 3; experiential layer 0.

**Pages and what they supplied**: association journal page (aims, abbreviation, news items); association editors page (29 entries); association journal-operations pages for 2025 and 2024 (acceptance figures); archived Sage author-instructions page (2025-07-16; HTML comments removed before reading, none held policy text); archived Sage aims and editorial-board pages (2022-12-03); Sage publisher policy pages (AI, prior publication, data, ethics, independent researchers, archiving, Sage Choice list).

**Experiential checks**: SciRev (https://scirev.org/journal/american-educational-research-journal/): journal page exists, no reviews, popularity score only. LetPub: the public search URL returned only its landing page, so no journal row. 小木虫 / 知乎: one web search for the journal name with 投稿经验 审稿周期 拒稿 returned no muchong or zhihu thread; fabiaoji not reached. Reddit: one web search for the journal with submission experience, review time, desk reject and reddit returned no thread. Zero first-hand reports found.

**Read in a real browser 2026-11-24:** https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/AER (live; the 50 double-spaced page limit and the 100-120 word abstract are unchanged from the 2025-07-16 copy; a keyword search of the live text found no AI wording; its Sage Choice section says gold open access is subject to a publication fee) and https://journals.sagepub.com/editorial-board/AER (live board: 131 entries, 1 Editor-in-Chief, 7 Co-Editors, 19 Associate Editors, 1 Managing Editor, 88 Editorial Board members and 15 Student Editorial Board members, 1+7+19+1+88+15 = 131; 111 entries print a country, of which USA 102, Germany 2, and one each for Colombia, Chile, Belgium, Turkey, Norway, New Zealand and Australia (102+2+7 = 111), and 20 entries print an institution without a country). Real browser not done in the time box: https://journals.sagepub.com/home/AER ; https://journals.sagepub.com/aims-scope/AER ; the association's Standards for Research Conduct and Code of Ethics and the Reviewer Guidelines.

**Unreadable pages**: none of the two Sage pages read above is still unreadable; the home and aims pages stay covered by the archived copy of 2022-12-03.

**Fields deliberately left blank, and why**: CiteScore, desk rejection rate, all four review-cycle times, special issues, transfer policy, reviewer-report publication, R+R rounds, reviewer recommendations, word-limit negotiability, read-and-publish list, under-review preprint rule, reviewer competence and quantitative-bias rows (no first-hand source). Impact factor and quartile: paywalled, not stated by policy.

**Method note**: `scripts/import_openalex.py` produced the scaffold. Keyword counts come from a paged OpenAlex works pull (233 records, 2 requests at about 2-second spacing, no key, no 429), reconstructing abstracts from OpenAlex's inverted index and applying the regexes listed above locally. Crossref supplied year counts, issue numbers and author lists. The Sage price list was an XLSX read with openpyxl.

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Length**: the main document may not exceed 50 double-spaced pages including references, tables, figures and notes (Format; archived guidelines 2025-07-16). Longer files may be returned.
- **Anonymisation**: identity, affiliations and funding must be removed from everything outside the title page, own work cited as "Author, year", and the revision response letter anonymized (Format, Practical Concerns; archived guidelines).
- **Prior publication**: manuscripts previously published, in press or under consideration elsewhere are not accepted (Preprint Policy; archived guidelines).
- **Abstract**: 100-120 words (Format).
- The live guidelines page was re-read in a real browser on 2026-11-24 for length, abstract and AI wording only; the other rules above rest on the 2025-07-16 copy.

### Soft Tax

- **Selectivity signal**: the association reports 4.7% accepted in 2025 (34 of 720) and 4.4% in 2024 (36 of 812) (Metrics; https://www.aera.net/tabid/22227/mid/55753/default.aspx). These are the association's own approximate calendar-year figures.
- **Open access cost**: gold route costs USD 3,640 (2026 list) after acceptance (Open Access).
- **Preprint and anonymity**: a posted preprint may reveal the author to reviewers, per the Sage page (Preprint Policy, Practical Concerns).
- **Time**: no decision-time figure exists on any page read; the tax cannot be quantified (Review Cycle Time).

### Best Suited For

- Empirical education studies, quantitative or qualitative, on schools, teachers, policy, achievement and higher education: `school` 60.27%, `polic(y|ies)` 29.22%, `teacher` 26.94%, college terms 19.18% of 219 abstracts; interviews 11.87%, experimental terms 8.68% (Subject Density, Methodological Preferences).
- Equity-focused and race-attentive work: racial terms in 56 of 219 abstracts (25.57%) and equity in 31 (14.16%) (Sensitive Topics, Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Causal and large-scale quantitative designs alongside qualitative work: causal-design terms 5.94%, longitudinal 9.59%, case study 9.13% (Methodological Preferences).
- Authors without a university affiliation: Sage's independent-researcher policy welcomes them and an award notice names an independent-scholar AERJ author (Practical Concerns); this says nothing about acceptance odds.

### Not Recommended For

- Authors needing a short or conceptual piece: the limit is 50 double-spaced pages, and `philosophical` and meta-analysis or review terms appear in 0 of 219 abstracts (Format, Methodological Preferences); the data show absence, not rejection.
- Autoethnography or self-study approaches: 0 of 219 abstracts (Methodological Preferences).
- Anyone who needs a verified turnaround or a first-hand review account before choosing: none exists in the sources read (Review Cycle Time, AI-Research Notes).

### Rejection Fallback Chain

> No source states where rejected authors usually go. The rows below are topical neighbours that already exist in this corpus, listed only because they share the subject area (education research) or the same association; they are not a claim about acceptance odds or fit.

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Educational Researcher](educational-researcher.md) | Same association (AERA) and subject area; an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
| 2 | [British Educational Research Journal](british-educational-research-journal.md) | Same broad subject area (education research); an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
| 3 | [Teaching and Teacher Education](teaching-and-teacher-education.md) | Teacher-focused empirical overlap (teacher terms appear in 59 of 219 abstracts here); an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
